title: leucanthemum vulgare subsp. subalpinum
intro: Leucanthemum vulgare subsp. subalpinum, commonly known as Alpine Daisy, is a subspecies of the Oxeye Daisy plant, characterized by its small white flowers and slender stems. The Alpine Daisy has been used in traditional medicine to provide various health benefits, including reducing inflammation, improving digestion, and supporting the immune system. Its therapeutic actions include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, which can help to soothe wounds, reduce fever, and prevent infection. The bioactive constituents of the Alpine Daisy include flavonoids, terpenoids, and sesquiterpenes, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential uses in treating various health conditions.
